title: Letters and Vow Revisited
premise: Emrys Halloran returns to her family's coastal vineyard for her grandmother's eightieth-birthday reunion, dreading the questions about her stalled writing career and her ex. To deflect, she recruits Callum Reyes—a charming stranger she meets at the ferry dock—to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. But Callum turns out to be the vineyard's new consulting vintner, hired by her grandmother, and their fake romance collides with real feelings neither planned for. As old letters from Emrys's late grandfather surface revealing a hidden first love and a broken vow, Emrys must confront why she keeps every relationship in past tense—including the one with herself. She ends the novel by reading her truth aloud at the harvest dinner, choosing Callum not as an escape from her story but as a partner in writing its next chapter.
about_author: Jude Thornbury is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who spent a decade writing letters she never sent before turning them into fiction. She lives on the Atlantic coast, where she still walks the cliff path at dusk and insists every good love story needs salt air.

chapters.title: The Ferry Bargain
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Crossing to Saltmere Island for her grandmother's reunion, Emrys panics over the interrogation awaiting her and impulsively asks the handsome stranger beside her to be her fake boyfriend for the weekend. He agrees with disarming ease. The beat: guarded humor masking loneliness; she believes she's controlling the story.

chapters.title: Vows and Vine Rows
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. At Halloran Vineyard, the stranger introduces himself—Callum Reyes, the new consulting vintner her grandmother hired. Trapped by her own lie, they agree to keep the act going through Sunday's toast. The beat: mortification curdling into reluctant alliance; first spark of genuine curiosity.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Helping Nana sort the attic for the birthday display, Emrys finds unsent letters from her late grandfather to someone named 'L.'—evidence of a secret first love and a vow he never kept. The beat: shaken faith in the family's tidy legends; her cynicism about love acquires a wound.

chapters.title: Dessert Was the Turning Point
chapters.summary: POV: Callum. During the reunion dinner, Callum plays his role too well—defending Emrys against her critical aunt, remembering details he shouldn't know. By dessert the performance feels dangerously real to him. The beat: rising tension; Callum realizes he's falling while knowing the whole thing expires Sunday.

chapters.title: Bluffing the Bluffs
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. A stolen afternoon walking the cliff path to the decommissioned lighthouse blurs the line between act and truth—they share real confessions disguised as 'character backstory.' The beat: intimacy achieved under cover of fiction; both begin lying to themselves instead of each other.

chapters.title: The Letter L
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Emrys discovers 'L' was Lily, her grandmother's late sister—and that Nana has known about the letters all along. Confronted gently, Nana admits she chose loyalty over truth for fifty years and regrets the silence more than the betrayal. The beat: theme crystallized; Emrys sees her own avoidance mirrored across generations.

chapters.title: Harvest Pressure
chapters.summary: POV: Callum. First frost threatens the grapes, and Callum works nights while Emrys, feeling sidelined, overhears him telling Nana the weekend was 'just a favor.' Wounded, she reverts to invisibility and prepares to leave early. The beat: midpoint collapse; miscommunication weaponizes her oldest defense.

chapters.title: Past Tense
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Packing to go, Emrys rereads her own abandoned manuscript and recognizes the heroine who never lets anyone stay. She confronts Callum; he admits he fell for her and never knew how to say so without breaking the terms of their bargain. The beat: raw honesty replaces performance; forgiveness of self begins.

chapters.title: The Toast at First Harvest
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. At the harvest dinner, called upon to toast, Emrys abandons the script: she reads one of her grandfather's letters aloud, then claims her own truth—her failures, her fear, her feelings for Callum—in front of everyone. The beat: climax; public vulnerability as the ultimate act of loyalty to herself.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Weeks later, Emrys stays on to finish her novel in the restored lighthouse cottage while Callum brings in the vintage. They write new vows—not of permanence promised, but of honesty kept daily. The beat: resolution; love chosen in present tense, identity reclaimed, the mirror finally forgiven.
